{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI / Company Site Development and Hosting Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Review findings and proposed redline positions 
**Prepared for:** Customer (the "Company") — counterparty HDI ("Vendor")

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is workable — New York governing law, a revenue-share fee model with no minimum commitment, no non-solicit, and an MFN and promotional undertaking that run in our favour — but the risk allocation is materially incomplete for a deal in which HDI develops and hosts a consumer-facing Site under our brand and processes our customer and order data.

Three protections are absent altogether: there is **no indemnity**, **no limitation of liability or damages exclusion** anywhere in Sections 1–10, and **no allocation of ownership** of the Site work product or the customer data generated through it. Separately, Section 4.2 imposes an **uncapped, formula-driven Termination Payment on us alone**, geared to 50% of our own Net Sales above $800,000 and payable over eight quarters, with no exception where we terminate for HDI's default — a penalty on the customer that also undercuts our Section 6 exclusivity exit and our 90-day convenience right. Section 6.1 also restrains **our** business well beyond the branded Site, reaching undefined "products substantially similar" to Deerskin Products.

Secondary but substantive gaps: no performance or conformance warranty (Section 9 is limited to corporate reps), no post-termination transition assistance or data return, no insurance covenant, an unlimited-frequency audit right in Section 3.4, a bare successors clause in Section 10.3 with no consent standard, a Section 1.4 access grant that omits affiliates and contractors, a 90-day non-renewal window, and silence on venue in Section 10.5.

We have prepared redlines for each item below. We recommend leading with the three critical omissions and the Section 4.2 penalty.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section (as reviewed) | Issue / our position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language exists despite HDI hosting a branded Site and handling our customer data. Insert HDI indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard procedure and a narrow reciprocal Company indemnity limited to our Content and our breach of law. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) | The Agreement allocates control (5.2), merchant-of-record status (5.3) and a Marks licence (6.1) but never allocates ownership of the Site, HDI's work product for us, or the customer, order and user data. New Section 5.5 confirms our ownership (work product assigned to us), HDI retains its pre-existing platform and grants us a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded HDI materials; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | No cap, damages exclusion or aggregate-liability language anywhere in Sections 1–10; both parties face unlimited exposure. Insert mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement); Company payment obligations excluded from the cap. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 4.2 imposes an uncapped payment on us alone on any termination by us — 50% of our Net Sales above $800,000 over eight quarters — with no HDI equivalent and no exception for HDI default. Replace with our fallback: fee capped at three months' payments, as the sole termination amount, disapplied where we terminate under Section 1.6, for HDI's material breach, or by non-renewal. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 6 grants HDI exclusivity over our branded consumer web channel for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit (only the 70-day launch right in 1.6 or a 90-day termination triggering the Termination Payment). Add automatic termination of exclusivity and freedom to procure from third parties if HDI misses launch or fails to operate the Site and does not cure within 30 days. HDI's reciprocal restraint in 6.3 benefits us and is unchanged. |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 6.1 restrains us from any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or undefined "products substantially similar," reaching beyond the branded Site (only carve-out in 6.2 is closeout merchandise). Narrow to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer site during the term, with carve-outs for our other channels, internal development and acquisitions. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 | Our convenience right requires 90 days' notice and triggers the Section 4.2 Termination Payment, while HDI may exit on the same 90 days at any renewal point. Reduce our notice to 30 days without penalty and confine HDI's convenience right to the end of a term (the penalty itself is addressed at item 4). |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause with no consent standard, so HDI could assign development and hosting of our branded Site — potentially to a competitor of the type named in Section 6 — while our affiliate/M&A rights are unprotected. Add our affiliate/successor assignment right, confirm no change-of-control right for HDI, and require our consent (not unreasonably withheld) for HDI assignments, never to a competitor. |
| 9 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | The Section 1.4 grant of access to HDI's system and administration tools runs to "the Company" alone — no affiliates or contractors, no irrevocability during the term, no successor transfer. Add affiliate/contractor scope, irrevocability during the term (subject to our uncured material breach) and transferability to an M&A successor. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 9 contains only corporate existence, authority and no-conflict reps; no warranty that the Site will be developed, hosted or maintained to any standard and no remedy (only the 70-day launch right in 1.6). Add workmanlike-performance, 12-month conformance, compliance-with-law and no-malicious-code warranties with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund. No disclaimer to carve out. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 | Section 4 covers only term and the termination payment; nothing requires HDI to return our Content, customer and order data or to assist migration, and the Section 10.7 survival list omits data return. New Section 4.3: up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of data in machine-readable form within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter, no withholding of data as leverage. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 3.4 already gives 30 days' notice, business-hours access, scope limited to payment records and HDI's cost, but frequency is unlimited with no confidentiality obligation or exclusion of system access. Add once-per-12-month cap, confidentiality hook to Section 8, no-system-access statement, and 5% underpayment cost-shift. |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 | Automatic 12-month renewals with a 90-day non-renewal window (at the outer edge of our walk-away line) and no reminder; renewal pricing (30% revenue share) is otherwise acceptable. Add a 30-day opt-out right for us and a 60-day pre-renewal reminder from HDI, with no charge for non-renewal. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 | New York governing law is our preferred position and there is no arbitration clause, but Section 10.5 is silent on venue. Add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, without otherwise altering the sentence. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 1.4 | The only "no less favourable" undertaking runs in our favour: Section 1.8 obliges HDI to promote our Site and Products no less favourably than its own catalog titles, at HDI's cost. No obligation on us to extend best terms or match third-party offers. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 1.4 | Fees are a revenue share on actual Net Sales above a monthly threshold; no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap on us. (Section 4.2 is addressed at item 4.) No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 | No non-solicitation, no-hire or inducement restriction. The only personnel provision (Section 5.4, General Managers) is a liaison mechanic imposing no hiring restraint on us — consistent with our preferred position of no non-solicit. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 | No insurance covenant, yet HDI hosts our consumer-facing Site on its own servers and processes our customer and order data. New Section 10.9 with baseline limits (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M while HDI processes our customer data, workers' compensation as required by law) and certificates on request. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

We should not sign without resolution of the following:

1. **HDI indemnity (item 1).** HDI builds and hosts a consumer-facing Site under our brand and handles our customer data with no defence or hold-harmless obligation of any kind. We need indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct.
2. **Limitation of liability (item 3).** The Agreement is silent, leaving both parties with unlimited direct and consequential exposure. A mutual cap with the standard uncapped carve-outs is required.
3. **Ownership of Site work product and customer data (item 2).** Absent Section 5.5, HDI would by default claim the deliverables it develops for us and hold our customer, order and user data with no licence back.
4. **The Section 4.2 Termination Payment (item 4).** An uncapped, one-sided payment geared to our own Net Sales, applying even where we terminate for HDI's default, is a penalty on the customer and must be capped at three months' fees and disapplied on HDI default, non-renewal and Section 1.6 termination.
5. **Data return on exit (item 11).** We cannot accept a structure in which our customer and order data can be withheld as leverage; return, deletion and transition assistance obligations are a condition of signature.

Related leverage points we expect to trade rather than walk on: the Section 6.1 restraint on our own business (item 6), the performance-based exclusivity exit (item 5), and the 30-day convenience right (item 7).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** to HDI covering all 15 deviation/missing items, flagging items 1–4 and 11 as walk-away and marking the three compliant items (15–17) as accepted as drafted, so they are not reopened.
2. **Sequence the negotiation:** first pass on the three critical omissions (indemnity, liability cap, IP/data ownership); second pass on the Section 4.2 penalty together with the convenience, exclusivity-exit and non-compete narrowing, which are commercially interlinked.
3. **Confirm with the business team** the 12-month fees figure used for the liability cap and the three-month figure for the capped termination fee, and whether six months is sufficient transition assistance for a Site migration.
4. **Request HDI's certificates of insurance** against the item 18 baseline limits, and confirm which HDI entity will host and process customer data for purposes of the cyber limit.
5. **Confirm HDI has no competitor-assignment plans** and secure the Section 10.3 consent standard before signature; identify the competitor list we will name.
6. **Diary the renewal mechanics** once agreed (30-day opt-out plus 60-day HDI reminder) so the window is not missed if the 90-day construct survives negotiation.
7. **Offer the fallbacks** in the redline where sensible — capped termination fee in lieu of the Section 4.2 formula, and narrowed field-of-use in lieu of deleting Section 6.1 — to keep the exclusivity bargain intact while removing the customer-side penalty.

*All section references above are as they appear in the reviewed document; no findings or conclusions beyond those verified in review have been included.*"}
